transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (NovaSec CTO), Marta Rios (Infra Lead), Samir Patel (ML Eng)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): discussed on-prem install for air-gapped environment, driver compatibility, offline license activation, runtime tuning. Agreed to deliver artifacts and run benchmarks.

[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this pretty technical. Quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Jordan (NovaSec): Jordan here. Marta and Samir on my side.
[00:00:15] Marta (NovaSec): Hi all.
[00:00:18] Samir (NovaSec): Samir here.
[00:00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya from Redwood, SE on runtime and deployment.
[00:00:26] Alex: Cool. We're planning to cover three main things: artifact delivery and verification for an air-gapped install, the offline license/token flow, and then runtime perf tuning — batching, kv-cache warmup, and quantization recommendations. Sound good?
[00:00:40] Jordan: Yep. Our main constraints are: no outbound egress from the inference tier, locked-down bastion for artifact staging, and we have a baseline P95 latency target of ~120ms for our chat endpoint.
[00:00:50] Priya: Perfect. We'll be explicit about the install bundle and the checksums, and we have an offline activation that uses a signed license blob — no call-backs required.
[00:01:05] Samir: A few specifics: our nodes are DGX-like boxes with A100s, RHEL8 family, and some older drivers in prod currently. We can stage updated drivers but need the exact versions pinned.
[00:01:20] Priya: Understood. For A100 we typically support NVIDIA driver 525+ with CUDA 11.8/12.1 depending on runtime. We will provide a driver compatibility matrix; note if you plan to use latest cuBLAS/cuDNN optimizations we recommend 535/12.2 but we'll map to the kernel you have.
[00:01:40] Marta: We run a custom kernel (4.18-ish) backport for RHEL8. Anything to call out there?
[00:01:45] Priya: That can matter for the runtime's low-latency DMA paths — we'll check compatibility. We'll flag any kernel modules needed.
[00:01:55] Alex: Quick interjection on licensing: the offline license is a signed blob tied to your cluster-id and expires per the term. We also offer a 90-day evaluation offline token if you want to pilot.
[00:02:06] Jordan: We'll take the 90-day eval if possible.
[00:02:10] Alex: Good. We'll issue that after you provide a cluster fingerprint.
[00:02:14] Samir: On the runtime side — can you explain the KV cache warm-up strategy? Our workload has a high proportion of long chats, recurring prefixes, and a lot of token-level reuse.
[00:02:25] Priya: Sure. Two parts: prefix/persistent KV cache and dynamic per-request KV cache. For on-prem we can enable persistent prefix caching which survives restarts — it's stored in a fast local store on node SSD and keyed by prompt-hash. That avoids re-running the full prefix for common system messages. The other is continuous batching with KV sharing where we keep the key/value tensors in GPU memory across requests.
[00:02:47] Samir: Do you evict by LRU? We want predictable memory usage.
[00:02:50] Priya: Yes LRU with configurable thresholds. You can cap the total KV bytes on a per-GPU basis; when cap hit it evicts least-recently-used entries. Also we surface metrics for cache hit-rate so you can correlate with latency.
[00:03:05] Marta: How do we seed the cache for a pilot so the first-run isn't terrible?
[00:03:10] Priya: We provide a cache seeding tool in the tarball. It can precompute KV shards for your canonical prompts and load them into the local store. Offlined -- you can run it over your prompt corpus prior to turning on production traffic.
[00:03:26] Alex: Note: when we say KV "cash" in some docs, it's a typo — it's KV cache.
[00:03:30] (laughter)
[00:03:33] [00:03:35] Jordan: On batching: we need to balance latency vs throughput. What's Redwood's guidance for batch size and dynamic batching windows?
[00:03:45] Priya: For chat where tail latency matters we recommend dynamic batching with micro-batch windows of 5–10ms for low-latency configs, or 20–50ms if you can tolerate more latency to reduce per-token cost. We have adaptive batching: the runtime adjusts batching window to maintain target latency SLOs.
[00:04:05] Samir: Does adaptive batching play nicely with KV cache sharing? I'm worried about cross-request interference.
[00:04:10] Priya: The runtime isolates KV contexts per conversation; batching only coalesces independent requests at the kernel level. We maintain per-conversation KV pointers so sharing is read-only across similar prefixes but not mixing states.
[00:04:25] Marta: For quantization: we want to drop to int8 if possible. Any recommended profiles? Accuracy loss concerns for reranking vs generation tasks.
[00:04:33] Priya: We provide three quant profiles: safe (FP16 activations, FP16 weights), aggressive (int8 with per-channel scales), and mixed (weights int8, activations FP16). For generation we recommend mixed first; for strict reranking where scores matter, safe or a calibrated int8 with post-calibration checks. We'll share an accuracy vs throughput chart.
[00:04:56] Alex: Also note there are model-specific suggestions — e.g., Llama-derivatives tolerate int8 well, some encoder-decoder models less so. We'll include per-model notes in the bundle.
[00:05:07] [00:05:10] Jordan: About the install artifact: how is it signed? We can't have a package that could be tampered.
[00:05:16] Priya: The tarball will be signed with a Redwood PGP key and include a SHA256SUMS file. We also provide an optional offline attestation file: a signed manifest of installed binaries and expected checksums to be validated by a local verifier.
[00:05:30] Marta: Can we run the verifier as non-root?
[00:05:34] Priya: Yes, verifier runs as user in the staging area and only requires read access to the tarball and checksums. Installation steps that require root are separate and documented.
[00:05:44] Samir: If we have an HSM, can the offline license be encrypted with our public key?
[00:05:50] Alex: Yes we can support an optional envelope encryption for the license blob; send a public key and we'll wrap the license so only your HSM can open it.
[00:05:58] Jordan: Good.
[00:06:00] [00:06:10] Priya: Shifting back to perf: for your P95 120ms target, we need to tune three things: model size selection, quantization, and batching windows. Also sequence length distribution matters — what's your average token length?
[00:06:23] Samir: Typically 80 tokens but spikes to 400 in long threads.
[00:06:28] Priya: For spikes we recommend a hybrid route: route short sequences to a low-latency profile (FP16 + small batch window) and long sequences to a throughput profile (bigger windows, quantized weights). Smart routing is in our on-prem runtime policy config.
[00:06:42] Jordan: Can routing be per-tenant? We have internal vs. external workloads with different SLOs.
[00:06:46] Priya: Yes, you can define routing policies by header, tenant, or endpoint. On-prem policy engine is local; no external decisioning required.
[00:06:55] [00:07:00] Marta: We asked about driver versions earlier. Can you send a matrix and also vendor fallback if we need ROCm for AMD?
[00:07:07] Priya: We'll include NVIDIA 525/530/535 + CUDA 11.8/12.1/12.2 mappings and a ROCm matrix for supported AMD cards. Note: some kernel tweaks are needed for ROCm on RHEL8; we'll list those.
[00:07:20] Alex: We'll also include a short script to detect conflicting drivers and recommended uninstall order so you don't end up with mixed driver blobs.
[00:07:28] Samir: Great. About the benchmark harness — what metrics will you produce out of the box?
[00:07:33] Priya: Latency histograms (P50/P90/P95/P99), throughput (tokens/s), GPU util, GPU memory usage, cache hit rate, and cost estimate per 1M tokens (estimation based on cycle counts). We'll provide a CSV and a small dashboard JSON you can view locally.
[00:07:51] Jordan: Will the harness run in air-gapped mode?
[00:07:54] Priya: Yes. It's a standalone binary in the tarball. You can feed it a prompt set and a rate profile; it will log to local files.
[00:08:02] [00:08:10] Marta: How long do you recommend the warm-up to get stable KV cache hit rates?
[00:08:14] Priya: Depends on your corpus, but we typically see converged hit-rate in ~5k requests for common prefixes. If you seed cache, that drops to warm (<100 requests).
[00:08:25] Samir: Is there any persistent eviction cluster-level so caches don't diverge across nodes?
[00:08:30] Priya: No cross-node KV sync by default — it's local-by-node design for latency. If you need global prefix sync we can provide an optional sync tool that ships precomputed shards to other nodes during maintenance windows.
[00:08:44] Jordan: Ok. We're worried about driver and kernel mismatch causing subtle SM hangs. Any recommended smoke tests?
[00:08:51] Priya: We include a smoke test suite: small model load, single-token echo, KV persistence test, driver stress microbench. It exits non-zero on any mismatched ABI. Run it after driver install and before large deploy.
[00:09:05] Alex: We'll share that in the README.
[00:09:08] [00:09:15] Samir: A few gotchas we've encountered in other stacks: calloc/numa pinning and docker vs. baremetal. Do you recommend containerized runtime or baremetal?
[00:09:24] Priya: Both supported. For strict latency you might prefer baremetal or a minimal container with --gpus=all and host networking. We recommend explicit NUMA pinning for multi-GPU nodes; our install script can emit suggested pinning configs based on nvidia-smi topo.
[00:09:41] Marta: We do use CRI-O rather than docker. Any issues?
[00:09:45] Priya: CRI-O is fine; ensure the runtimes support GPU plugin and that you mount /dev/nvidia* and the libraries. We'll include CRI-O notes.
[00:09:55] [00:10:00] Jordan: On the security side, audit logs: are there local audit trails for inference requests? We need per-request traces for compliance.
[00:10:07] Priya: Yes, local audit logs with configurable retention. We can redact inputs if needed and keep metadata (latency, model, token counts) always. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM via syslog or kept locally.
[00:10:18] Samir: And SSO? We'll integrate with our existing SAML provider for console access.
[00:10:22] Alex: On-prem console supports SAML/SAML2 and OIDC; we'll provide config examples in the runbook.
[00:10:30] [00:10:40] Priya: Wrapping up, we'll provide: signed tarball, checksums, driver matrix, offline license blob plus envelope option, benchmark harness, cache seeder, and smoke tests.
[00:10:52] Jordan: Timeline?
[00:10:55] Alex: We'll aim to get the tarball and harness to you by 2025-09-19. Can you validate driver inventory by 2025-09-20?
[00:11:02] Jordan: Yes.
[00:11:05] [00:11:10] Marta: A couple of smaller clarifications — can the installer run in a dry-run mode so we can audit file writes first?
[00:11:16] Priya: Yes, installer has a --verify-only flag that unpacks to a staging dir and runs the checksum/verifier without touching systemd units.
[00:11:27] Samir: For performance experiments, are there toggles for prefix caching TTL?
[00:11:31] Priya: TTL is configurable per-prefix namespace. We'll include suggested defaults.
[00:11:36] [00:11:40] Alex: Anything else?
[00:11:42] Jordan: One more — our legal wants a minimal offline EULA for the eval token. Is that doable?
[00:11:47] Alex: Yes we'll attach an eval EULA PDF with the token.
[00:11:50] [00:11:55] Priya: Alright, we'll follow through on the items. Thanks everyone.
[00:11:58] Jordan: Thanks.
[00:12:02] (call ends)
